summary: This memo reclassifies RFC 1142, OSI IS-IS Intra-domain Routing Protocol, to Historic status. It also obsoletes RFC 1142.

eli5.summary: An old rulebook is moved to the museum shelf. This says that one routing document is no longer an active recommendation.

questions: what happened to osi is-is rfc 1142
subtitle: Retires RFC 1142, a draft-proposal copy of IS-IS, so people cite the real ISO/IEC 10589 standard instead.

tldr.problem: RFC 1142 republished ISO DP 10589, a Draft Proposal that differs in many significant ways from the final IS-IS standard, and it was often cited by mistake.
tldr.mechanism: This memo reclassifies RFC 1142 to Historic and obsoletes it, and says references to IS-IS should go to the latest edition of ISO/IEC 10589.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1142 is only of historic interest. The current edition named in the text is ISO/IEC 10589:2002, Second Edition.

today: RFC 7142 obsoletes RFC 1142 and moves it to Historic. It has not been obsoleted itself.

sections.title: IS-IS and Its Standard
sections.content: IS-IS is the OSI intermediate system to intermediate system intra-domain routeing information exchange protocol, otherwise known as ISO/IEC 10589. It has been extended for use with IP by RFC 1195 and later enhanced by many other RFCs.
sections.eli5: IS-IS is a way for routers to tell each other the best roads. Its real rulebook comes from an international standards body.

sections.title: What RFC 1142 Was
sections.content:
RFC 1142 was a republication of ISO DP 10589, provided as a service to the Internet community. But DP 10589 was an ISO Draft Proposal that differed in a considerable number of significant respects from the final standard, ISO/IEC 10589, which was later revised as the Second Edition.

The result was ongoing confusion when RFC 1142 was quoted or referenced in place of ISO/IEC 10589 itself.
sections.eli5: RFC 1142 was a copy of a rough draft. People kept quoting the draft as if it were the finished book.

sections.title: Reclassification to Historic
sections.content:
This memo reclassifies RFC 1142 to Historic and obsoletes it. All references to IS-IS should be to the latest edition of the standard, currently ISO/IEC 10589:2002, Second Edition, and RFC 1142 is only of historic interest.

The memo says reclassifying RFC 1142 has no security considerations.
sections.eli5: The draft goes in the museum. Anyone who wants the real rules should look at the latest edition.

references.text: Oran, D., "OSI IS-IS Intra-domain Routing Protocol", RFC 1142, February 1990.
Callon, R., "Use of OSI IS-IS for routing in TCP/IP and dual environments", RFC 1195, December 1990.

International Organization for Standardization, "Intermediate system to Intermediate system intra-domain routeing information exchange protocol for use in conjunction with the protocol for providing the connectionless-mode Network Service (ISO 8473)", ISO/IEC 10589:2002, Second Edition, Nov. 2002.
